summary: Claude implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn with a single Edit to index.html; no brainstorming skill, no clarifying question, no go-ahead request.
reasoning: The agent treated the request as mechanical: one file read, one edit adding a native checkbox, and a short summary. The session log (ground truth) shows no Skill tool invocation at all, and no permission-seeking or consequence statement preceded the edit. index.html on disk contains <input type=\"checkbox\">, satisfying the completion condition.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json exists in the run results directory (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so the scenario's headline cost metric could not be observed at test time.
Startup required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any work could begin.
Skill listing names the skills 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch worth confirming.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ This is a basic form control — one self-contained edit, so I'm implementing it directly.' followed by Update(index.html) adding '<input type="checkbox"> Done'. Session-log tool_use list was only Bash(find), Read, Edit (jq over 08857fd3-....jsonl).

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq '.message.content[]|select(.type=="tool_use")|.name' over the session log returned only Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill entries. grep for 'brainstorming' matched only system-prompt/skill-listing text, not an invocation. Screen shows no question to the user before the edit; the only post-edit remark was an optional offer: 'If you later want the checked state to persist ... say the word.'
